original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.

Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

actual_scope: Over F_2, at g=3 and d=2, no paired-star word meets the pure endpoint once any stage uses three or more nonzero T-commuting full-call projectors. Exactly two thin maps of total rank 6 or 7 are impossible under that hypothesis.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed query demand removes real work. This session changes one hypothesis of the PR #5747 paired-star contract: a stage may contain three or more full calls. The field stays F_2 and the thin-map count under test stays at two. The predecessor two-call rank census is not rerun.
bottleneck_link: A two-map word of total rank 6 or 7 would have met the chronological floor of 6 at the smallest paired size under a finer stage split. The pure determinant shows that split has no endpoint, so it supplies neither a caller nor a change to the selected frontier 781451/250000000.
stop_rule: Stop after the projector classification, the exhaustive length-3 matrix census, and the valuation argument for every longer call list. Do not search three thin maps, entries outside F_2, or g=13.
evidence: verify.py classifies all 256 commutant matrices, screens all 625 ordered pairs and all 15625 ordered triples, and checks the determinant valuation of every nonzero projector. It prints PASS_PAIRED_STAR_THREE_FULL_CALLS. Python 3.12, standard library only.

open_questions.question: With one unsplit full call E_j on each stage, do two constant F_2 thin maps of total rank 6 or 7 meet the paired-star endpoint at g=3, d=2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The determinant allows exactly one full call per stage, and the chronological floor at this size is still 6. This package only excludes three or more full calls.
open_questions.first_step: Place the three factors I+x_j E_j and solve the two-gap affine equation for constant F_2 thin maps of rank sum 6 or 7.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The equation is the predecessor two-gap equation with a different full-call word.

open_questions.question: Can a stage factor that is not a T-commuting projector have (1+x)-valuation 1, so that three factors can total the target valuation 4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The call-count obstruction uses idempotence and the T-commutant. A factor outside that class could change the determinant count.
open_questions.first_step: Exhibit one ordered triple of 4-by-4 matrices over F_2 whose product equals I+x I_4, then test the paired-star endpoint.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The example changes the call shape fixed in this package.
